definitions.explanation: A large retail store carrying a wide variety of goods organized into departments. The formal term for what is more casually called デパート.

examples.japanese: {駅前|えきまえ}の{百貨店|ひゃっかてん}で{買|か}い{物|もの}をした。
examples.english: I shopped at the department store in front of the station.

examples.japanese: {老舗|しにせ}の{百貨店|ひゃっかてん}が{閉店|へいてん}することになった。
examples.english: A long-established department store is going to close.

examples.japanese: {百貨店|ひゃっかてん}の{地下|ちか}{食品|しょくひん}{売|う}り{場|ば}は、いつも{賑|にぎ}わっている。
examples.english: The basement food floor of the department store is always bustling.

notes:
USAGE:
More formal than the commonly used loanword デパート. Often used in news, business contexts, and official names. Major Japanese department stores include {三越|みつこし}, {伊勢丹|いせたん}, {高島屋|たかしまや}, and {大丸|だいまる}. The {地下|ちか}{食品|しょくひん}{売|う}り{場|ば} (basement food hall), nicknamed デパ{地下|ちか}, is a distinctive feature of Japanese department stores.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {百貨店|ひゃっかてん}{業界|ぎょうかい} (department store industry)
- {大手|おおて}{百貨店|ひゃっかてん} (major department store)
- {百貨店|ひゃっかてん}の{売|う}り{上|あ}げ (department store sales)
